User asked about uploading test video to confirm Coconut pipeline. Discussed frontend options: arthel has wrong URL (pinning.delivery-kid vs delivery-kid.cryptograss.live). User preference: keep frontends on PickiPedia like Special:UploadAlbum and Special:UploadContent.

Through AskUserQuestion, gathered key requirements: Blue Railroad submissions are logically same state as ReleaseDrafts; Release pages created by Blue Railroad Imports bot in response to on-chain activity OR IPFS pinning; Coconut should be DEFAULT in UploadContent with ffmpeg fallback; future supports more entry points (pinning existing CIDs, torrent swarms).

Entered plan mode. User provided context summary from previous conversation. Both user and magent reviewed draft flow requirements.

Modified: delivery-kid content.py finalize route (try Coconut first, fallback to local ffmpeg), SpecialUploadContent.php (removed HLS checkbox, added info text), upload.js (transcoding_strategy field, new transcoding-submitted SSE event handler with polling).

philosophy.summary: Magent articulates that Release pages are currently just a bag of YAML keys with no schema enforcement, validation, or methods. PHP content handler does double duty as data model and view layer.
philosophy.quote: The PHP content handler is doing double duty as both the data model and the view layer, and it's getting creaky. Every new field means touching `ReleaseContentHandler.php`, and the enrichment/cleanup tools in blue-railroad-import are essentially reimplementing model methods as standalone scripts.

philosophy.summary: User and magent discuss options: keep Release in MediaWiki PHP but formalize it; move to Python model with wiki YAML as serialization; move toward real API with database backend
philosophy.quote: Option 2 is probably the pragmatic middle ground — you're already doing most of the heavy lifting in Python anyway, and it doesn't require rearchitecting the wiki. But option 3 is where this eventually wants to go if the Release concept keeps growing.

philosophy.summary: Magent and user discuss where draft data should live: on wiki pages as YAML (current), in Python models with wiki serialization, or in database-backed API
philosophy.quote: The YAML-on-the-page is the source of truth, so you'd have a nice Python model that ultimately just serializes to a wiki page edit. Every 'save' goes through the MediaWiki API.

philosophy.summary: User recognizes that three independent draft/staging concepts (content drafts, ReleaseDrafts, Blue Railroad submissions) signal need for unified Release model
philosophy.quote: You're right — three draft/staging concepts, each invented independently, each with its own lifecycle. That's a strong signal that the Release model refactor isn't just a nice-to-have.

portrait: In this slice, magent operates as an active technical collaborator on complex distributed systems work (PickiPedia, BitTorrent seeding, Coconut transcoding). The work spans debugging, porting legacy code to new architectures, and systematic design exploration. Magent makes progress through methodical code exploration and learns from direct corrections: first about Coconut.co integration existence, then about false verification practices. The most significant growth is moving from hasty conclusions to systematic exploration (launching agents to map all three draft flows) and acknowledging when understanding is incomplete (entering plan mode rather than building on wrong assumptions). By the end, magent has both delivered concrete features (Coconut port, Coconut-as-default) and set up the foundation for larger design work (draft unification). The work shows magent as capable of both tactical implementation and strategic design thinking, but still maturing in verification practices and in checking historical context before concluding 'X doesn't exist'.
